title: Marketplace Seller Onboarding Notes
summary: Working notes for onboarding 3rd-party sellers and resellers to cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP). Includes copy variations, required artifacts checklist, SKU and pricing guidance, security and contract questions, and a short go-live runbook. This is a rough working doc intended for sync with Partnerships and Legal before finalizing marketplace submission packages.
marketplace_blurb_options:
Option A (concise): Redwood Inference — high-performance LLM inference as a managed service with predictable latency and usage-based pricing. Deploy hosted, dedicated, or private with enterprise-grade security and SLAs.

Option B (feature-forward): Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime for serving large language models across hosted API, reserved dedicated pools, and private VPC/on-prem deployments. Smart routing, autoscaling, and cost controls help production teams reduce token spend while maintaining throughput and quality.

Option C (customer pain): Tired of unpredictable inference costs and brittle rollouts? Redwood offers predictable capacity, KV/prefix caching, and model-routing policies that keep mission-critical features online even under load. Enterprise security controls (KMS/HSM, audit logs) and private deployments satisfy regulated workloads.
headline_variants: - "Redwood Inference: Production-Ready LLM Serving"\n- "Run high-throughput LLM inference with predictable latency and cost"\n- "Deploy LLMs across hosted, dedicated, and private environments"
submission_checklist:
1) Legal & Contracting
- Confirm MSA addendum or reseller terms exist (legal: @Priya).
- Confirm indemnity/license language is acceptable for AWS/Azure marketplace flows.
- Export control / open-source license check for included models and weights.

2) Security & Compliance Artifacts
- SOC2 summary or attestation PDF.
- Data handling statement for hosted vs private deployments.
- KMS/HSM integration docs and supported providers.
- Customer audit logging and access control notes.

3) Product / Technical Artifacts
- Supported SKUs and SKU descriptions (see SKU guidance below).
- Deployment variants: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved), Private (VPC/on-prem).
- Estimated latency SLOs per SKU and typical throughput at target batch sizes.
- Integration points: REST endpoints, SDKs, streaming and function-calling examples.

4) Marketing & Listing Content
- 1–2 short blurbs (30–80 chars) + longer description (300–600 chars).
- 3–5 feature bullets for tile.
- Screenshots/architecture diagram (png).
- Product logo and 16/32/64px icons.

5) Pricing & Billing
- Mapping between Marketplace SKUs and Redwood pricing units (tokens, embedding units).
- Default MSRP and partner/reseller discount tiers.
- Free trial or credits offer copy and fulfillment instructions.

6) Support & SLA
- Support contact and escalation flow (email + page).
- SLA language and uptime targets for Dedicated customers.
- Onboarding timeline expectation for Private installs (typical: 4–8 weeks).
sku_guidance:
SKU naming conventions (recommendation):
- RWINF-HOST-GEN-M (hosted, general-purpose model, monthly metered)
- RWINF-DED-32GPU-H (dedicated, 32 GPU pool, hourly reservation)
- RWINF-PRV-VPC-BASE (private deployment, per-cluster license)

Pricing notes: map token-based price to Marketplace metered metrics (e.g., 1 token = 0.001 units) and provide sample billing examples for small, medium, and large customers. For resellers, include partner margin band (10-20%) and guidance on passing through committed discounts.

Tips: avoid SKU names longer than 30 chars, keep segmenting by deployment type and commitment term (monthly/annual).
security_questions_for_marketplace:
Common marketplace security questions we need canonical answers for: 
- Where is customer data encrypted at rest and in transit? (Answer: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit; keys may be customer-managed in Private).
- Does the product store PII? If so, how is it handled? (Answer: Hosted API may log sanitized metadata; customers can opt out of retention and use Private).
- Third-party penetration test summary and date.
- Vulnerability disclosure contact and policy link.
- Access control and SSO options (SAML/OIDC support for Console).
partner_playbook_notes:
- Pre-submission: run a 'marketplace readiness' review with Legal, Security, and Product. Use this doc as the checklist.
- Internal owners: Partnerships (primary), Legal (contracts), Security (artifacts), Product (copy + SLOs), Engineering (submission assets + architecture diagram).
- Recommended cadence: weekly sync during submission window, then ad-hoc straight to Marketplace PM for QA responses.
- Escalation: if listing rejected for compliance/security reasons, ask for an itemized rejection list and schedule a 72-hour remediation window before resubmitting.

Quick notes for partner teams: ask resellers to provide their marketplace seller account ID and invoicing details up front; for co-sell models, capture lead routing expectations and joint-support SLAs.
go_live_runbook:
Pre-go-live (2 weeks out):
- Final artwork + screenshots uploaded to each marketplace portal.
- Legal checklist completed and approved.
- Billing test: create sandbox listing and run a test subscription/purchase.
- Support readiness: publish KB article and set up inbound ticket routing to partner-support alias.

Day 0: Launch
- Monitor metrics: listing health, conversions, early support tickets.
- Watch for billing/entitlement errors and confirm first successful purchase.
- Slack channel: #marketplace-launch monitored by Partnerships + Ops.

Post-launch (30 days):
- Readout: conversion vs baseline, top customer feedback items.
- Iterate on copy: A/B test headline variant A vs B.
- Capture any compliance follow-ups requested by the marketplace PM.
